title: Tech Note: Repairing Corrupted Structures with 4D Insider
author: Achim Peschke, Manager of Support Department, 4D Germany
featured_technology: USERS TO BLOB / BLOB TO USERS commands

historical_commentary.text: This note explains 4D Insider's approach to 'repairing' a corrupted 4D structure file by moving all uncorrupted objects, in a strict order (lists, tables, then everything else), from a damaged source database into a fresh destination database, thereby rebuilding the data dictionary rather than literally repairing it. It is deeply tied to 4D 2004-era Design Mode concepts (binary structure files, Trash, groups/folders, the Explorer) and the standalone 4D Insider utility, which have evolved significantly or been superseded since; structure corruption recovery workflows in modern 4D versions rely on different, more automated tooling. The step ordering discipline it describes (numbering integrity, references) is a good illustration of how fragile binary structure files were in that era, a concern much reduced by modern data formats.
related_updates: 4D Insider as a standalone repair tool from this era has been superseded by newer recovery/verification tooling in later 4D versions
4D's binary structure file format and repair workflows have evolved considerably since 4D 2004
Project Mode (introduced in 4D v17, 2018) uses text-based project files, changing how structure corruption and recovery are approached compared to the binary .4DB era described here
